brief.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix plunge 7-9% on global chip selloff; ₩392tr Chungcheong capex unveiled as memory pricing plateaus
brief.summary: <cite index="20-1,20-8">Samsung Electronics tumbled more than 7% while SK Hynix sank over 9% at the open, wiping out billions in market value as Asia's largest chipmakers bore the brunt of the global tech selloff</cite>. <cite index="22-1,22-3,22-17">SK Hynix will invest about 100 trillion won to build NAND flash memory and advanced packaging fabrication plants in the region, while Samsung plans to invest about 140 trillion won in the Chungcheong region</cite>. <cite index="13-4,18-2,18-7">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 93–98% QoQ in Q1 2026, with Q2 forecasts showing 58-63% increases for DRAM and 70-75% for NAND Flash</cite>, but <cite index="13-22">DDR4 and DDR5 spot prices both kept climbing—the mainstream DDR4 1Gx8-3200 chip rose 3.57% in a week to $34.80—but suppliers' higher quotes had made buyers hesitant to chase further increases, thereby limiting actual procurement demand</cite>. <cite index="28-4,28-9">SK Hynix passed Samsung Electronics to become South Korea's most valuable listed company, with shares climbing more than 280% this year, pushing its market value above $1 trillion</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: Relative value flipped on SK Hynix's Nasdaq IPO filing (SKHY ticker, up to $29.4B raise, July 10 target) and HBM dominance (~50-55% share vs Samsung's 35-40%). SK overtook Samsung as most-valuable Korean public company for first time in 26 years; today's 9% selloff vs 7% Samsung drop reflects higher beta but fundamentals favor SK: faster HBM4 qualification, locked NVIDIA supply through 2027, and Indiana packaging plant breaking ground. Samsung's ₩140tr Chungcheong HBM fab announcement is defensive catch-up. Near-term, pair narrows on profit-taking after 730% SKH vs 350% Samsung 12-month runs; medium-term, SK's 3:1 wafer conversion penalty (HBM crowds out DDR5) is shared pain but SK monetizes at 5-6x premium. Watch Samsung HBM4 Broadcom/Google TPU qualification as only re-rating catalyst.

memory_cycle.notes: Q1 2026 DRAM contract +93-98% QoQ marked cycle peak velocity; Q2 deceleration to +58-63% signals rate-of-change inflection. Spot momentum broke in early June: buyers stopped chasing, NAND trading went quiet despite green prints. DDR4 spot now $2.10/Gbit vs HBM3E contract $1.70/Gbit—an inversion indicating legacy scarcity, not demand strength. HBM3E sold out through 2026, but 20% 2026 price hikes (Dec 2025 reports) already reflected in forward quotes. Structural: AI consuming 20% of global wafer capacity; HBM 3:1 conversion ratio compresses commodity DRAM indefinitely. Tactical: no new fab capacity until Micron Idaho (2027), Samsung/SK modest line expansions only. Demand destruction visible in buyer hesitation but not yet in contract reversals. Call: prices stay elevated through Q3 2026, sequential increases slow to single digits, first YoY declines unlikely before mid-2027.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-1,1-9,1-10">HBM3 costs approximately $200 per 24GB stack, HBM3E costs ~$300 per 36GB stack; supply remains constrained through 2026 with lead times for HBM3E stacks at 20-26 weeks</cite>. <cite index="4-3,4-22">HBM3E contract pricing is approximately $13–17 per GB as of early 2026, down from a peak of $17–20/GB in H1 2025</cite>, but <cite index="6-1,6-3">Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix raised HBM3E supply prices by nearly 20% for 2026</cite> following H200 China export approval. <cite index="1-2,1-4,2-17">SK Hynix leads with 50-55% market share, followed by Samsung at 35–40% and Micron at 5–10%</cite>. <cite index="31-16">HBM supply is fully allocated through 2026, including HBM3E</cite>. <cite index="6-8">Analysts forecast next year's HBM revenue mix will be approximately 55% HBM4 and 45% HBM3E, with HBM4 beginning in Q3 to rapidly absorb demand</cite>. Allocation chokepoint remains binding constraint on AI accelerator shipments.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix plunge 7-9% as Nasdaq tech rout spills into Asia; KOSPI recovers from -3.4% to -0.2% after capex briefing
news_pulse.implication: Profit-taking after 350% (Samsung) and 730% (SK Hynix) 12-month rallies; high index concentration (50% of KOSPI weight) amplifies volatility but government industrial policy support (₩392tr commitment) cushioned close. Risk-off contagion, not Korea-specific.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix files for up to $29.4B Nasdaq listing under SKHY ticker, targeting July 10 debut; 10 ADSs per ordinary share
news_pulse.implication: Largest-ever Korean cross-listing; newly issued shares (not secondary) fund Indiana $4B packaging plant and capacity expansion. Validates HBM premium valuation; foreign institutional access widens shareholder base. Watch pricing vs. Kospi parity for arb signals.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix CEO announces ₩100tr investment: M17 NAND fab (₩80tr, 1H 2029 start) + P&T7 advanced packaging (₩20tr)
news_pulse.implication: Addresses NAND supply gap (enterprise SSD demand +70-75% QoQ Q2 contract pricing) and secures CoWoS-alternative packaging for HBM. Cheongju becomes NAND hub; construction begins 2027. Long lead time (3 years) means no near-term capacity relief but locks ₩100tr gov't subsidy commitment.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung pledges ₩140tr Chungcheong investment for HBM fab, packaging, OLED, batteries (Electro-Mechanics ₩8tr, SDI ₩9tr)
news_pulse.implication: Political capex theater (President Lee Jae Myung present) but commits Samsung to domestic HBM capacity race. HBM fab targets Broadcom/Google TPU qualification gap vs SK's NVIDIA lock. Packaging investment mirrors SK's P&T7; signals 2027-28 HBM4 ramp necessity.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contract prices +93-98% QoQ Q1 2026, +58-63% forecast Q2; NAND +70-75% Q2, outpacing DRAM for first time this cycle
news_pulse.implication: NAND acceleration reflects enterprise SSD prioritization (AI infrastructure); DRAM deceleration vs Q1 suggests peak velocity passed. NAND now rising faster than DRAM = capacity reallocation working as intended. Expect Samsung/SK NAND ASP tailwinds Q2 earnings but gross margin compression if spot cracks.

news_pulse.headline: DDR4 spot $2.10/Gbit now exceeds HBM3e contract $1.70/Gbit; buyers hesitant to chase further increases despite +3.57% weekly gains
news_pulse.implication: Inversion = legacy fab shutdowns faster than demand decay; marginal buyer balking at spot levels. Spot stall while contract still rising = early demand destruction signal. If spot rolls over in July, contract follows in Q3. Samsung/SK insulated by long-term agreements but 2H pricing guidance at risk.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity ramping from 75-80k wpm to 120-130k target by end-2026; both CoWoS-L and CoWoS-S fully booked, 52-78 week lead times
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS remains binding bottleneck for HBM-based AI accelerators; NVIDIA locked ~60% of 2026-27 expansion. SK Hynix P&T7 and Samsung packaging investments are TSMC-dependency hedges. Packaging constraints > HBM constraints > wafer constraints in AI supply stack.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex consensus $400B+ (AWS, Azure, Google, Meta); 40-50% flows to AI silicon, driving HBM/CoWoS sold-out status through 2027
news_pulse.implication: Sustained AI infra build validates Samsung/SK capex cycle through 2027; hyperscaler custom silicon (Trainium, TPU, Maia) still relies on HBM. No demand-side risk visible; supply gating only. Confirms memory makers' pricing power persists 18+ months.

brief.derivatives_signal: KOSPI 200 futures likely gapped down at open mirroring ADR weakness (SSNLF, HXSCL OTC); intraday recovery from -3.4% to -0.2% suggests institutional support at government briefing marked the low. Options flow unavailable but implied vol spike expected given 7-9% single-day moves after extended rallies. SK Hynix Nasdaq listing (July 10 target) creates cross-market arb opportunity if SKHY ADSs price tight to KRX ordinary shares; watch premium/discount to Kospi for institutional rotation signals. Samsung/SK weighting at 50% of KOSPI (up from 25% YE 2025) means index options now de facto memory sector bets. Near-term: profit-taking continues until Nasdaq stabilizes; next support Samsung ₩285k, SK Hynix ₩2.25m.
watch_for_next_3h: Nasdaq futures direction into US open—Samsung/SK correlation to SOX index tightened; further Nasdaq weakness extends Asia selloff into Europe
SK Hynix SKHY Nasdaq listing pricing/timing updates—any delay past July 10 or pricing below ₩2.5m KRX equivalent signals risk-off
TrendForce or DRAMeXchange spot pricing updates for DDR4/DDR5—if spot rolls over (negative weekly print), validates demand destruction thesis and pressures 2H guidance
Hyperscaler (AWS, Azure, Google) commentary on memory procurement or capex adjustments—any pushback on $400B+ 2026 spend would crack HBM/DRAM pricing assumptions
